| id  | name  | role         |

to_markdown_table.note: a generator renders normally: records is materialised once up front, so a one-shot iterable is not spent collecting the columns
to_markdown_table.output:
| id  | name  | role         |

to_markdown_table.note:
pipes are escaped and newlines become
, so one record always stays on one row
padding counts characters, not screen columns, so the wide CJK cell overflows its padding — the markup is still valid and renders aligned, only this raw text looks ragged
no records and no columns= leaves no columns to resolve, so there is nothing to render
an empty resolved column list is the trigger, not empty input: _rows has two records and the result is still empty
a single record on its own is refused rather than iterated as its keys; wrap it in a list
to_markdown_table.output: TypeError: records must be an iterable of record dicts, not a single dict; wrap one record in a list

to_markdown_table.note: a bare string would silently become one column per character, so it is refused; pass ['name']
to_markdown_table.output: TypeError: columns must be a sequence of column names, not 'name'; pass a list such as ['name']
